# ULI2 reference corpus

`uli2_tiny.uli` is a 2-second synthetic stereo album encoded by the sibling
`gba-audio` C encoder. It is deliberately varied: two-tone stereo, silence, a
noisy band, and high-frequency clicks. It is 39,308 bytes and 129 frames
(including the frame-0 preroll), at 32,768 Hz, one track.

`uli2_tiny_expected.txt` is the frozen expected-vector file, originally pinned
against the normative C reference decoder. It records, for every frame:

- the FNV-1a 32 hash of the 512 L + 512 R int8 samples;
- the FNV-1a 32 hash of the 512 L + 512 R int16 samples;
- bits consumed, bit position, every `UliOps` counter, the reference cycle
  model, and the cumulative `xover`/`hfnz` diagnostics;
- the album-wide hashes.

The Rust test (`tests/reference_corpus.rs`) compares every field, then exercises
`seek_track`, `seek_entry`, malformed albums, and short output buffers.

The expected file is now regenerated by the Rust tool
[`crates/uli-lite/examples/gen_expected.rs`](../../examples/gen_expected.rs),
not by `gen_expected.c`. That tool uses the portable `uli-lite` decoder, so it is
a **maintenance / snapshot** tool, not an independent oracle. The committed file
is the authority; do not regenerate it merely to make a failing decoder test
pass.

## Regenerate

The `.uli` source fixture is still produced by the temporary `gba-audio` C
encoder. From this directory:

```sh
GBA_AUDIO=${GBA_AUDIO:-../../../gba-audio}

python3 gen_fixture.py
make -C "$GBA_AUDIO/encoder"
"$GBA_AUDIO/build/uli_enc" \
  --album tiny.f32 --tracks tiny.tsv --out uli2_tiny.uli \
  --budget 300000 --threads 1
```

Then regenerate the expected vectors from the repository root:

```sh
make uli-fixture
```

or directly:

```sh
cargo run --manifest-path crates/uli-lite/Cargo.toml \
  --target <host-triple> --example gen_expected -- \
  crates/uli-lite/tests/fixtures/uli2_tiny.uli \
  crates/uli-lite/tests/fixtures/uli2_tiny_expected.txt
```

The fixture is committed so `cargo test` / `make uli-test` do not need a C
compiler or the encoder. `gen_fixture.py` is general Python tooling and remains
allowed; the C encoder is the temporary encoder of record until the Rust encoder
lands. See [`ULI2.md`](../../../../ULI2.md).
